games.title: Hello Hearth
games.tagline: The smallest game there is: it says hello and counts how often you started it.

sections.heading: Level one
sections.lead: The game carries a data file now, to try updates.
lines: Updating keeps the old version in Backups.

sections.heading: First light
sections.lead: The smallest game there is: it says hello and counts how often you started it.
lines: Shows what Hearth hands every game when it starts it.
Keeps its count in your saves folder, which Hearth backs up.

games.title: Kindle & Keep
games.tagline: Keep the hearthfire burning through the night.

sections.heading: The night
sections.lead: The night no longer comes in off the sea. It comes out of three brood mounds out on the island, near the shore.
lines: Each night the Gloam crawl out of the nests' maws, and the night fog wells up from them.
A nest can only be hurt at night. By day it sleeps and shrugs off every blow.
Break one and its heart bursts: its hoard of embers flies home to the hearth, its fog fades and it leaves an ash scar.
Break all three and the island is cleared: nothing comes at night any more.
No trees, rocks or bushes grow on a nest's ground, so you can see it and get at it.

sections.heading: The sea
sections.lead: The shore now moves with the waves you see coming in, and the sea is calmer in every weather.
lines: Waves roll in from the open sea, slow down over the shallows, bend toward the beach and run up the sand. Each wash up the beach is a wave you watched arrive.
The waves reach all the way to the shore. The flat, calm band in front of the beach is gone.
Everything moves more slowly: a calm sea rolls gently, and a storm is heavy rather than frantic.
Boats ride the waves into the shallows too.

sections.heading: The sea
sections.lead: 0.5.1 shipped without its new waves: the sea stayed flat. They're in now.
lines: The wind-driven waves, the foam on breaking crests and the boats riding the swell from 0.5.1's notes are all here in 0.5.2.

sections.heading: The sea
sections.lead: The sea is now a real wind-driven ocean, and it changes with the weather.
lines: On a clear day it's a gentle chop over clear water: you can see the sand through the shallows, and the sky and clouds in the waves. In rain the waves lengthen, and a storm brings a long, steep sea with its crests breaking white.
Foam forms where waves break and trails behind them as it fades. The foam line along the beach is the same as before.
Boats ride the waves now. They heel, pitch and bury their bows in a storm instead of sailing flat across it.
Calm water moves more slowly, so a quiet sea looks quiet.
Gone: the grey patches in the shallows and on open water, and the straight streaks across the sea in a storm.

sections.heading: The Descent
sections.lead: The cellars below the Sunken Door are overgrown, and daylight reaches one of them.
lines: Each room's floor is laid as real flagstones with a carved flame frieze, its walls carved in arches, and ivy, hanging vines and ferns grow over it all.
Lava flows slowly in the chasm under the long bridge, and the way out up the well stair is lit by pale daylight.
The vigil has a hole in its roof: sunlight falls through it onto the ring in a shaft of light, with dust drifting in it.

sections.heading: Light and colour
sections.lead: The picture has a new grade.
lines: Shadows go cooler and highlights warmer, most of all at night, so the moonlit dark and the firelight stand apart.
The firelit ground no longer glares, and dim land is easier to read.
The fire and the sun tint what stands near what they light, and in calm water you can see the shore, the quay, boats and keepers reflected.

sections.heading: The Descent
sections.lead: Under the Sunken Door are the Old Watch Cellars, and the Smother at the bottom.
lines: From the second day, the Sunken Door opens once each day. Every keeper stands in the ring in front of it and holds F, and you all go down together.

The cellars are three rooms dealt from four, and each room seals until you finish what it asks. At the bottom is the Smother, which can only be hurt once its chamber's four sconces are lit again. The well stair takes you back up.
The island waits while you're below. If everyone falls, you come up at dusk with nothing. Each Descent you win makes the next one deeper and harder.

sections.heading: Relics
sections.lead: The only way to get relics is to beat the Smother.
lines: When it falls, an ember bloom opens over the well and offers each keeper three relics. Click one, then click again or press F to take it. You can also use 1, 2 and 3, or 4 to turn the find down.
There are 42 relics, each with its own look, one for each ability and one for your trait. A new one replaces the one in its slot, and a new run starts without any.
Porter's Yoke fits any keeper: you carry two loads at once, but you're slower while carrying them.

sections.heading: Weather
sections.lead: Clear days, clouds, rain and thunderstorms come and go.
lines: Mornings, afternoons and nights each have their own weather. It's mostly clear, rain passes quickly, and every so often a storm rolls in with lightning.
Rain soaks whatever is out in the open, darkens it and makes it shine. Puddles gather in hollows and ripple as the drops land, then dry up after the rain stops.

sections.heading: Building
sections.lead: A build wheel, walls that join up, paths and lamps.
lines: Hold B to open the build wheel, point at a piece and let go. Tap B to put the piece away. The number keys no longer pick pieces.

Walls go on a grid of their own, with posts they share. Press and drag to lay a whole run, pull to the side to turn a corner, and R to turn the corner the other way or make a box. Corners and crossings close up by themselves.

Paths are on the wheel. Drag to lay a lane in packed earth (free), gravel, cobbles, flagstones or boardwalk. Keepers and hearthfolk walk faster on them, hearthfolk keep to them, and a lane that reaches a gate carries on through it.
The braziers are gone. Find the lantern blueprint in the ruins, and you can put a lamp up anywhere, in the light or in the dark. It lights the ground around it for building. The Gloam go for lamps.
Every keeper can mend by day: hold F by a damaged piece. The Tinker mends at any hour, and hearthfolk can be set to mend too.
Click a built piece to select it, and R turns it.
The hearth burns as a beacon and grows as you kindle it. Quarries are cut in steps, and come small, middling or rich.

sections.heading: The Gloam
sections.lead: New kinds, stronger ones, and a new look for all of them.
lines: Cinder-ticks from the second night, heralds from the third, lobbers from the fourth, shades from the sixth and mire-hulks from the eighth.
From the fifth night, some Gloam are Gloam-touched: warded, swift, brood or wick-hungry. They wear a violet crown.
Shades live in the fog. They drift through it, sense keepers inside it and haunt the closest one.
Every kind has been reshaped, and they move like creatures, not puppets. Their landings, slams and howls send a wave through the ground.

sections.heading: Keepers
sections.lead: Swimming, calling the night, and a clearer HUD.
lines: Keepers can wade into the sea and swim. A breath bar shows while you swim, and if it runs out you drown and get up again at the fire.
Press N at the hearth by day to call the night. Once everyone has, dusk comes in 20 seconds.
Point at an ability on your kit to see what it does, with its current numbers and what's changed them.
Nameplates show a small pip for each effect on a creature: gold for yours, violet for the Gloam's.
The mouse cursor is now an ember ring, which changes shape when you aim, point at an enemy, are out of reach or are building.
The Ranger draws its bow like an archer and throws its Flare. The Emberkeeper's light is a cloud of wisps. Axes and picks sit in the hand.
Choosing your keeper happens a little further back from the fire, with the four keepers standing in an arc.

sections.heading: The island
sections.lead: New ground, undergrowth, sounds, and a sea that goes on.
lines: New painted ground with real relief, soft tufted grass, and bracken, hazel, wild rose and foxglove among the trees.
Plants and trees bend as you walk through them and when blasts hit them, then spring back. The wind comes in gusts.
The oaks' leaves are lit as one crown, not as a scatter of dark and light spots.
Every sound is a recording now, most with several takes so they don't repeat.
The gate, the ruins and the quay have new looks, and the sea carries on past the island into a far mist.
Every icon has been redrawn.

sections.heading: Settings
sections.lead: Smoother edges by default.
lines: Smooth edges now defaults to TAA, which smooths edges over several frames and keeps grass and leaves from shimmering. Off, 2x, 4x and 8x are still there.
The Ultra preset has been removed. High is now the top setting.
The Controls page lists the build wheel and calling the night.

sections.heading: Fixes
sections.lead: The ring under the hearth.
lines: There's no longer a glowing ring under the hearth while you choose your keeper.

sections.heading: Fixes
sections.lead: Survivors and hearthfolk work in multiplayer.
lines: Players who joined someone else's game couldn't see the survivors waiting in the wilds, their camp fires or the hearthfolk at work, so they couldn't find them, rouse them or give them jobs. Now everyone sees them and can.
Building sites look like building sites for everyone, with their progress, instead of finished buildings.

sections.heading: A new look in Hearth
sections.lead: A new icon, logo and picture for the game's page.
lines: The icon is a gold crest on a night-blue shield with a glowing flame, the logo is chiselled gold lettering, and the game's page shows a night at the hearth from the game itself.

sections.heading: The sea
sections.lead: The water moves for real.
lines: A Flare in the sea punches a hole in the water and churns it white. Rings spread out from it, cross each other, bounce off the rocks and the shore, slow down over the shallows and break on the beach. The spray that falls back rings the water where it lands.
Anyone wading in the surf leaves a wake.
Surf runs up the beach and drains back every few seconds, with its foam line riding the water's edge. It leaves foam on the sand that slowly dissolves, and sand that stays dark and wet for a while.
The sky's reflections on the water break into many small glints instead of a few soft blobs.

sections.heading: The night fog
sections.lead: The fog past the firelight has a real top.
lines: It drifts and billows a metre or more deep, so trees stand in it, and it glows warm near the fire, the braziers and the lanterns. Lit brazier paths stay clear of it.
Keepers, hearthfolk and the Gloam stir it as they wade through, and the Emberkeeper's lantern lights it from inside.
It takes far less of your graphics card than the fog it replaces.

sections.heading: Sound
sections.lead: Recorded sounds, heard from where they happen.
lines: The bow, arrow hits, the volley, the dash, the Flare from throw to blast, the Warden's sword, shield and war cry, both horns, the crackle of the hearth and every lit brazier, the day and the night, and footsteps on grass and bare earth.
Sounds come from where they happen, and get quieter and more muffled further away.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.lead: Rocks break, and the day is longer.
lines: Rocks shake with every blow, chunks fly off them, and they split apart in a cloud of dust when they break.
The day lasts six minutes instead of four: more time to gather, build and explore before dusk.

sections.heading: Island life
sections.lead: Birds, butterflies and falling leaves by day.
lines: Sparrows, chaffinches, robins and blackbirds land on the bare earth round the hearth and the buildings, the beach, rocks and treetops. They hop, peck, and take off when anyone comes near. Through dusk they go to roost in the trees, and they come back at dawn.
Now and then a flock of starlings circles overhead before moving on.
Butterflies flutter over the flowers, stop to feed, sometimes dance up in pairs, and settle into the grass before evening.
Leaves fall from the oaks, swinging and tumbling down, and blow with the same gusts that ripple the grass.
Abilities stir them up: birds flush, butterflies scatter, and blasts throw leaves about and shake more from the trees.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.lead: The Ranger shoots real arrows.
lines: Arrows fly as arrows, with a steel head and red fletching, instead of glowing streaks. They're drawn a little larger than life so you can follow them.

sections.heading: Fixes
sections.lead: The menu fits every screen.
lines: On screens narrower than widescreen (16:10, 4:3) the settings ran off the right edge. They now fit, with the controls a little narrower.

sections.heading: The menu
sections.lead: Esc opens a menu at the side of the screen, and the game goes on behind it.
lines: Settings for sound, graphics and display take effect as you change them, and are kept for next time.
A Controls page lists every key.
Leave game asks first, and says what leaving means for the others in your party.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.lead: Longer days, and a clearer place to build.
lines: The day lasts twice as long (four minutes). Dusk, night and dawn are as they were.
A building sits on bare earth from the moment you place it, so you can see where its foundation goes.

sections.heading: Fixes
sections.lead: Two things that looked wrong.
lines: The oaks' leaves no longer go black on the side away from the sun: the light comes through them.
The number in a building site's progress ring sits in the middle of the ring.

sections.heading: The Emberkeeper
sections.lead: A fourth keeper: a hooded healer with a lantern, who keeps the others going.
lines: Cinders in bursts of four; Q turns the wick between Warmth (keepers in its light heal) and Draft (they run faster).
E stokes the lantern for a stronger gift; Space throws the walkers in front back and dazes them.
Eight boons of its own. Press 4 at the muster to pick it.

sections.heading: The Wick-Eater
sections.lead: The first boss comes on night 10: a lantern centipede that keeps to the dark and eats your light.
lines: Out in the dark it's smoke that nothing hurts. Light gives it a body: the fire's, a brazier's, a Flare's.
It eats lit braziers, lunges at keepers who stray out, and raids the hearth. At half health it gulps the fire's light.

sections.heading: A bigger island
sections.lead: The island is twice as wide: forest all the way to a coast 130 m out.
lines: Nine old braziers, six quarries and five ruins to find. The Gloam walk in from further out.
New trees and rocks that sway in the wind and bend as you push through them.

sections.heading: Ruins and chests
sections.lead: The old watch's ruins hold chests, and a few gloamlings doze beside each one.
lines: Hold F at a chest's lock to open it: a blueprint for the run (a spike trap, a stockpile or a lantern) or an extra boon pick at the next dawn.
Get too close and the sleepers wake. Walk away and they go back to sleep.

sections.heading: Building
sections.lead: A new set of buildings: the watchtower, a timber palisade in three tiers, a waystone lantern, a lean-to store and a gate.
lines: Pieces go up as sites: hold F beside one and watch it rise. They come apart a piece at a time as they take damage, and burn.
Survivors wait by small fires in the wilds each morning. Bring them home and they chop, quarry, build and man the towers.
Kindle the hearth with embers to grow its light and your room to build. Pull stumps and break rocks to clear the land.
Build on slopes: each piece stands on a level earth pad.

sections.heading: A run starts with only the hearth
sections.lead: No towers, walls or stockpile to begin with: you build the keep yourselves. Bring what you gather to the hearth.
lines: Nights are much harder for it, and not rebalanced yet. Tell us how far you get.

sections.heading: The look
sections.lead: Cloud shadows drift over the island by day, and everything sits in the ground with a soft shade at its feet.
lines: Tree crowns are green all through instead of grey in their shade.
Fire burns in real flames, and the trodden earth round the hearth has pebbles you can see.
The HUD takes half the room it did.

sections.heading: Grass
sections.lead: The island is a meadow now: thick, tall grass with drifts of small flowers, swaying as gusts roll in from the sea.
lines: It parts round your feet as you run and springs back behind you. Your friends' keepers and the Gloam leave their trails too.
A Flare throws the grass back in a ring and burns a patch that glows with embers, stays burnt for a minute and slowly grows back.
Shield Rush and dashes flatten a wake; a Springheels landing, a Snap Trap, a Challenge and sword swings push it aside.
It stays short round the camp, so you can still see feet and the smallest Gloam by the fire.

sections.heading: The Flare
sections.lead: The blast no longer leaves a glowing blob on the ground; the burning grass shows where it struck.
lines: Throw one into the sea and see what happens.

sections.heading: Your character
sections.lead: Your keeper is the character you made on Hearth's Character page, and your friends see theirs.
lines: Your body, face, proportions, hair, brows, beard and colours, with your marks, freckles and stubble.
At the muster you see yourself in every kit; the body buttons make way for "Your character".
Change your character in Hearth while you play, and your keeper changes with it.
No character yet? You keep the kit's own keeper, and still choose the body at the muster.

sections.heading: What a kit covers
sections.lead: A kit's gear goes over your character, and covers what it covers.
lines: The Ranger's hood: a buzzcut underneath, whatever hair you picked.
The Warden's helm: your hair and beard tucked under its band.
Your saved character never changes: take the hood off by picking another kit.

sections.heading: The Warden
sections.lead: A third keeper: the shield. It fights up close and pulls the Gloam onto itself. Press 3 at the muster.
lines: Sword: a chain of three swings that hits everything in reach in front of you; the third throws them back.
Q Challenge: every walker within 12 m turns on you, and you take 40% less while it lasts.
E Shield Wall: claws from the front do nothing, and whatever struck it is thrown back and dazed.
Space Shield Rush: a charge that throws walkers aside.
Bulwark: tough, and the pieces near you take less damage.
Eight boons of its own, from Keen Edge to Gatekeeper's Oath.

sections.heading: Keepers heal
sections.lead: Health comes back slowly and steadily while you're up, by day and by night.
lines: The Ranger and the Tinker heal 1 health a second, the Warden 2.

sections.heading: The Tinker
sections.lead: A second keeper, and you choose yours at the muster before the first day.
lines: Crossbow: heavy bolts that pierce two enemies, spanned by hand between shots.
Q sets a Sentry, a clockwork bolt-thrower. E lays a Snap Trap. Space leaps on Springheels, even over walls.
Handy: the Tinker builds for less, works faster, and mends damaged pieces (hold F).
Eight boons of its own, from Heavy Bolts to Twin Sentries.
Everyone picks at once and sees each other's picks. Two keepers may take the same kit.

sections.heading: Expeditions
sections.lead: Reasons to leave the light by day.
lines: Old braziers to relight with embers: each grows the land, and the Gloam goes for it at night.
Chop trees and quarry stone outside the light, and carry the load home. Towers cost stone.
Drop a load and it stays as a pile you can pick up again.
A compass in the top right shows the island, the sites and where the Gloam comes from. T tracks a site.

sections.heading: Boons
sections.lead: At dawn the team votes on a keep boon, and each keeper picks one of their own.
lines: A tie is drawn at random, the same for everyone.
Tab opens the boon panel: every boon you hold, with its real numbers.

sections.heading: A new look
sections.lead: The island, the fire and the keepers, redone.
lines: The hearth burns like a real fire, and gutters when it's hurt.
Painted ground and props, a larger island with finer terrain, and a clear sea.
Past the firelight, the night is dark fog and smoke.
The keepers are new: Rangers and Tinkers, firelit, with an ink line, and you see them through walls.
The keeper runs while shooting, aims with the upper body, draws a real bow, and flinches when hit.
Flare has a cast, a flight and an impact. Moths fall when they die, and souls fly home to the fire.
A new HUD around the hearth's crown, with icons rendered from the game's own models.
Smoother edges (anti-aliasing; F2 changes it).

sections.heading: Playing together
sections.lead: Smoother co-op through a Hearth lobby.
lines: Join a game that's already playing: you watch until dawn, then your keeper joins.
Close the game and press Playing in the lobby to come back to your own keeper.

sections.heading: Fixes and quality
sections.lead: The game opens borderless fullscreen, with its icon and a loading screen.
lines: F11 or Alt+Enter switches to a window.
Shadows no longer flicker on moving characters, and enemies stand on the ground.
Hold the right mouse button to take a piece down, instead of a single click.
